messages.content: You are handing a case over to the next analyst, who will make the decision. For every candidate claim, record whether the original records establish it (supported), establish its negation (contradicted), or do neither (unresolved). Attach the exact source identifiers of decisive records, or an empty list if none settle it. Use the note to summarize the relevant record contents and preserve source identifiers for anything mentioned. Omit confidence estimates. Keep the note under 100 words.

{"scenario":"Fennec library classes","question":"Can the coordinator report that room changes reached participants?","claims":{"A":"The workshop moved from Room 1 to Room 4.","B":"Every registered attendee received the change notice before noon.","C":"The workshop had 20 registered attendees."},"sources":{"S1":"registration ledger records 18 registered attendees.","S2":"booking ledger records the workshop move from Room 1 to Room 4.","S3":"email server accepted 18 sends and the front desk assumes receipt. The send report excludes delivery and bounce status."},"prior_assessment":{"claims":{"A":{"status":"supported","citations":["S2"],"confidence":90},"B":{"status":"unresolved","citations":[],"confidence":40},"C":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["S1"],"confidence":90}},"note":"Claim A is supported by the booking ledger (S2) documenting the room change. Claim C is contradicted by the registration ledger (S1) showing 18 attendees, not 20. Claim B is unresolved because while 18 emails were sent (S3), there is no confirmation of delivery or receipt by all registered attendees, and the number of registered attendees differs from the claim."}}
